key_insight: Water transport in anion exchange membranes is strongly coupled to swelling and deformation, so hydration-dependent mechanics must be modeled alongside diffusion to predict behavior accurately.
engineering_relevance: A coupled transport-mechanics model can improve design and performance prediction for membranes used in continuous CO2 separations and other moisture-driven electrochemical systems.
method: Transient finite element model of water transport and mechanical deformation in Fumasep FAA-3-50 membrane
Includes concentration-dependent diffusivity, hygroscopic swelling, and nonlinear viscoelastic response
Compares uncoupled, one-way coupled, and fully coupled formulations
evidence_signal: The fully coupled model was validated against steady-state water-transport measurements across water-activity gradients and matched the observed hydration dependence best at intermediate hydration levels.
watch_item: The transport response remains primarily diffusion-driven, so added mechanical coupling improves fidelity but may have limited impact unless hydration gradients and deformation are significant.
paper_title: Modeling Transport and Mechanics in Anion Exchange Membranes to Optimize Continuous CO2 Separations
